method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, type descriptor name, RTTI name and call target was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts come from the Lua 5.1 bytecode of the installed client scripts, parsed by a bytecode reader and evaluated by a stub interpreter where the declaration facts say so, and from scans of the executable named in each fact. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: How the retail client binds actor work tables to Lua and which natives a MyPlayer initialization reaches: the _bindWork helper path and the _bind flag of the work userdata, the work member type widths, the declared work layout of the MyPlayer chain (charaWork and playerWork) with its bind ids, and static Lua call contracts of fifteen native registrations of twelve Lua names (the shadowed _turnDir registration at order 60 is recorded under relatedNatives): _setTouchAttribute, _isTouching, _updateWork (CharaBase, GroupBase, DirectorBase and ItemBase), _lockLockonControl, _unlockLockonControl, _getGMRank, _getOrientation, _getMemberLocalizedDisplayName, _getOccupancyGroup, _getRegion, _getInstanceName and _turnDir. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish work member values, server packets or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.MEASURED: Counted or parsed by the method named in the fact, from the executable or from the Lua 5.1 bytecode of the installed client scripts.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

framework.reference: manifests/binding_map_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/fade_actor_group_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the type registry at 0x00CC9D60, the holder receiver adapter, cell tags, the world object chain and the yield request.

MyPlayer.note: Overrides the PlayerBase virtual slots that the thunk natives use.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar listed here has one rel32 caller in .text.

framework.holdersNote: Each invoke routine casts the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor. The holder constructors are reached through the functor copy routine that the wrapper calls. The wrapper bodies of the earlier contracts are recorded in their manifests.

pushers.0x00748B30: Control reference. INFERRED from the return list entry of _getOccupancyGroup.

cellTags.note: The readers were identified by the tag compare at the start of each. The list builders select registry entries by position: entry 0 int, entry 1 float, entry 2 bool, entry 3 Utf8String and entry 4 control. 0x0072B390 declares one float, 0x0072B5B0 one Utf8String, 0x0072C260 one control, 0x0072BDC0 an int and a bool and 0x0073CF80 two Utf8String and two int entries.

worldObject.chain: R is the address that 0x00CC7510 returns for ExecuteParameters +0x04. X = [R], Y = [X +0x04], W = [Y] and V = [W], the chain of the earlier contracts.

fields.Y +0xEC: Object that receives the _updateWork requests of CharaBase and DirectorBase through 0x00767FC0.
fields.V +0x17758: RaptureUserControl object embedded in V, vftable 0x00F90F64. Its dword at +0x40 is the counter that the lock-on slots 7 and 8 change.
fields.V +0x17838: CharaElement object read by 0x004D72F0. Its bytes at +0x45C, +0x45D and +0x45E are the armed, touched and reported attribute masks.
fields.V +0x4E0: Area object read by 0x004D7390. _getRegion reads its dwords at +0x94 and +0xAC, the first dword of the third and the third dword of the first of three 0x10 byte slots from +0x8C.

worldObject.tier: STATIC for the offsets and calls, INFERRED for the roles.

scriptSurfaces.kind: script method over an embedded Lua helper
scriptSurfaces.behavior: Sets w = r[workName] and w._bind = true. Walks w by key and by every trailing key except the last and assigns value under the last key, or under key when there are no trailing keys. Sets w._bind = false. Returns nothing.

scriptSurfaces.kind: script method over an embedded Lua helper
scriptSurfaces.behavior: Sets w = r[workName] and w._bind = true. Assigns the two element list {a, b} to w[member][1][key]. Sets w._bind = false. Returns nothing.

save.note: Uninitialized data in the file. No instruction stores to it by absolute address, so it reads 0.

poolKinds.sentinels: The dwords at 0x0130D788, 0x0130D78C, 0x0130D798 and 0x0130D79C hold -1. They are the no value sentinels of the index cells and of the bind record word.

facts.claim: The work userdata __newindex is the C function 0x00D2F000, which calls 0x00D175B0 with the stored work object. 0x00D175B0 looks the key up as a declared member through 0x00D16CD0. A hit calls the write path 0x00D272D0 with the member descriptor as the receiver. A miss compares the key with the six literals of the writeKeys table in order and stores nothing for _debug.

The _bind branch pushes stack index 3, converts it with 0x00CF35E0 and calls 0x00D12200 with ecx set to the pointer from the second closure upvalue (0x00D20490, the user data of upvalue 2). 0x00D12200 loads the dword that the pointer addresses and stores the converted byte at +0x48 of the object there. 0x00D12210 reads the same byte.

The write path 0x00D272D0 starts with 'cmp dword ptr [ebx],0' on the same pointer and returns without a store when the dword is zero. Otherwise it calls 0x00D12210 on that pointer. A zero byte takes the value route. Descriptor slot 0x6C converts the Lua stack top and writes it into the pool of the member for every pool kind. When slot 0x6C answered true and the key record kind byte at +0x2C equals the byte at 0x01377FB9 (save, 0), descriptor slot 0x04 (0x00D27400, a jump to 0x00CE4250) runs as a change notification that dispatches through the engine object at engine +0x218 (vtable +0x08) and then, when the storage dword at +0x14 is set, through 0x00D1A900. A nonzero byte takes the bind route, which calls descriptor slot 0x64 with the key record, the pointer, three index cells and the sentinel 0x0130D788 and stores no value. The key record is the work object +0x04. Its byte +0x2C is the pool kind that 0x00D16CD0 stored for the matched member and its byte +0x14 is a class level index.

Descriptor slot 0x64 is 0x00D27480 for every member type except timer, whose slot 0x64 is 0x00D25C50 ('ret 0x1C'). 0x00D27480 tests whether stack index -1 is a table (0x00CF3740). A table supplies two ints from its elements 1 and 2. Any other value supplies one int and the second int is -1. The three index cells reduce to one element index: -1 when the first holds the sentinel at 0x0130D78C, the first cell when the third holds the sentinel at 0x0130D79C, and otherwise third + first * second. A _bindWork write passes the sentinel cells, so the element index is -1. 0x00D25900 returns the member start (descriptor +0x08, in bits) plus, when the index is not negative, the index times the member width in bits (0x00D258E0). The routine takes the width from slot 0x0C divided by 8 and calls 0x00D12220, which jumps to 0x00CE67F0, with the first int as its first argument. 0x00D12220 has one caller.

0x00CE67F0 takes seven arguments: the id, a pointer to the kind byte (key record +0x2C), a pointer to the class level byte (key record +0x14), a pointer to the member start in bits, the second int, a pointer to the word source (always the sentinel 0x0130D788 on the bind route) and the span in bytes. It looks the id up in the hash table at 0x01377F20 through 0x00CE6E30, which hashes the key as the key xor 0xDEADBEEF. An existing entry whose dword at +0x10 equals the new start ends the call. An id with no entry is stored in that table (0x00CE6A6B..0x00CE6A7B) as the 12 byte bind record of workBinder.bindRecord. An id whose entry holds a different start leaves that entry untouched: the routine looks up or creates an entry in the table at 0x01377F48 through 0x006D1170, keyed by the receiver dword in ecx, and inserts the record into the hash table that entry holds at +0x0C (0x00CE68CE..0x00CE6A0B). The override is keyed on the start alone.

0x00CE5040 looks a key up through the table at 0x01377F48 and the hash table that the found entry holds at +0x0C, and otherwise in the table at 0x01377F20. Eight engine accessors call it: 0x00CE5290, 0x00CE53D0, 0x00CE5490, 0x00CE5540, 0x00CE5600, 0x00CE56E0, 0x00CE57D0 and 0x00CE58B0. Engine wrappers at 0x00CC7B90, 0x00CC7BE0, 0x00CC7C30, 0x00CC7CD0, 0x00CC7DE0, 0x00CC8580 and 0x00CC85C0 call six of them.

The reader at slot 0x1C of the boolean, integer8, integer16, integer24, integer32, float and uinteger64 descriptors begins with 'cmp dword ptr [edi],0' on the dword that the second argument addresses and pushes nil through 0x00CF33A0 (0x00DCE150) when it is zero. 0x00D16D40 passes the pointer from the second closure upvalue as that argument, so a member of an object with no installed storage reads nil.
The write path stores nothing when the pointer addresses a zero dword, so a write to a member of an object with no installed storage is dropped.

The width in bits of each member type comes from descriptor slot 0x0C. The string width is the dword at descriptor +0x10 added to itself three times, so eight times that dword. The bit widths are in the typeWidths table.

The factory 0x00D260D0 maps the type names to constructors. The boolean handler 0x00D1F2A0 and the integer8 handler 0x00D25640 allocate 0x10 bytes and construct the descriptor with 0x00D28390 and 0x00D28BE0. The string handler 0x00D25350 allocates 0x14 bytes, reads the length operand and constructs the descriptor with 0x00D2A3E0, which stores the length at descriptor +0x10.

The shared record keeps a per-pool vector of layout offsets and no member values. 0x00CE4550 forwards a read to 0x00CCB430, which indexes a vector at +0x0C of its receiver by the pool kind byte and calls virtual slot 2 of the pool object found there. 0x00CE48C0 forwards a write by pool kind to the virtual slot at +0x28 (save), +0x2C (temp) or +0x30 (sync) of the object at receiver +0x08.

For the six nested members of charaWork the declared nesting operand is at least the byte size of the declared members when each element is counted at its tag width, and equals it for eventSave (17 bits, operand 3) and eventTemp (67 bits, operand 9). For a receiver that is not the local player the operands are 64 and 16 for parameterSave and parameterTemp, which hold 336 and 48 bits.

The nesting operand is a capacity in bytes. The width slot 0x0C of the nesting and reserve descriptors (vftable 0x0110F8F4, derived 0x0110F974) is 0x00D25960, the string slot, which returns eight times the dword at descriptor +0x10. The constructors 0x00D23D10 and 0x00D23DA0 store the operand there, so the nested member occupies operand times 8 bits of its list. The eventSave and eventTemp operands equal the byte rounded laid out sizes (24 and 67 bits). An array member counts count times the element width in the laid out sizes, which is INFERRED because the code that applies a numeric third operand was not found.

0x00D1E0F0 lays out one declaration list with a running offset in bits that starts at an origin the caller passes. It builds the descriptor of each entry with the running offset as its start. Every descriptor constructor except boolean rounds that start up to a multiple of 8 bits with 0x00D1F4F0 and stores it at descriptor +0x08. The boolean constructor 0x00D28390 stores it unrounded. After the descriptor exists the routine adds the width of slot 0x0C to the running offset and, when the width is a multiple of 8, first rounds the running offset up to a byte. Booleans therefore pack to one bit each in declaration order and every other member starts on the next byte boundary. The result record holds the total bits at +0x00, the start of an _assignForChild entry at +0x04 and its width at +0x08.

The origin of a nested list is the start of its nesting member, so a nested member's recorded start is absolute inside the list that declares the nesting member. The nested list call passes the nested record +0x40, which the record constructor 0x00D1C100 fills from its third argument pointer, and the reader adds nothing but the record start to the level base, so the start must already include the nesting member's start. The local player and another player lay out the same ids at different starts after the nested members, which the per receiver table 0x01377F48 keeps apart. A top level list starts its origin at 0 and replaces it with eight times the sizes that 0x00D125F0 returns when the work object already has a declaration (0x00D166A9..0x00D166DE, not traced further).

The array count rule. A numeric third operand of a boolean or numeric tag does not reach the scalar creators (0x00D25640 and siblings read one argument, the start) and 0x00D1E0F0 adds one width per entry. The rule that an array occupies count times its element width is inferred from the nesting capacities: eventTemp holds integer16 x 4 and three booleans, 67 bits, in an operand of 9 bytes.

The shared record keeps a vector of vectors at +0x2C, one per pool kind. 0x00CE5BF0, called when a list is declared, resizes the vector of the kind to the level plus 2 entries, sets the entry of level plus 1 to the declared byte size plus the sum of all entries of the vector, and passes the size to the pool object through pool slot 1 (0x00CCB3F0). The base of a level is its entry in that vector, and the reader adds the byte part of the bit start to it. The bases of levels 0 to 2 are the plain prefix sums of the sizes. From level 3 each entry adds the earlier entries again, because the loop sums every entry.

The slot 0x6C bodies read the Lua stack top as the C API does. A boolean uses 0x00CF35E0, a wrapper of lua_toboolean (0x00DCDF50). An integer width and a float use 0x00CF35C0, a wrapper of lua_tonumber (0x00DCDED0): a number is used as is, a string goes through the string to number conversion 0x00DDE8B0 and 0x00DDE360, and any other value converts to 0.0. An integer width then truncates toward zero with the CRT routine 0x009D6636 and stores the low bytes of the width. A string member reads the value through 0x00CF3600. A numeric string written to an integer member stores its number and a non numeric string stores 0.

The first bind of an id is a global default and a bind of the same id to a different start is an override held under the receiver key, which the reader 0x00CE5040 prefers (STATIC). That the receiver is the work storage object of one actor, so that layouts with different nesting sizes under the same ids coexist per instance, is INFERRED. The callers of the engine wrappers and the packets that use bind ids were not traced. The ids declared by the scripts are the bindCalls table.

The initial value of a declared member before its first write. The readers return the pool bytes at the member start with no default, so the value is whatever the pool object of the kind holds. The class of the pool objects (vector at container +0x0C indexed by kind; slot 1 resize, slot 2 byte read, slot 3 byte write, slot 4 bit read, slot 5 bit write), their allocation and whether a resize zero fills were not found. The array index base of the member readers, which pass the index through 0x00D25900 without a visible subtraction. The meaning of _tag entries beyond the names and intervals that the scripts declare.

fields.name: classLevel
fields.use: index into the per kind layout vector at shared record +0x2C

fields.name: startBits
fields.source: descriptor +0x08 plus the element index times the width in bits; -1 element index leaves the start

fields.name: word
fields.source: 0xFFFF when the word source equals the sentinel 0x0130D788, which the bind route always passes

fields.name: spanBytes
fields.source: member width in bits divided by 8, 0 for a boolean

bindRecord.accessor: 0x00CE5290 takes the receiver, the id and two indexes. It starts from the dword at +0x04, adds spanBytes * index1 * 8 when the signed word at +0x08 is not negative and secondInt * index2 * 8 when index2 is above 0, then switches on spanBytes (1 to 4) to read 1, 2, 3 or 4 bytes through 0x00D11C70, 0x00D11CF0 and 0x00D11DB0 with the kind byte, the level byte and the bit position as pointers. A missing record answers -1. The word is -1 for every record, so index1 never applies.
bindRecord.address: base(kind, classLevel) + (startBits >> 3), bit startBits & 7, where base is the entry of the level in the per kind vector of the shared record

derivedBindStarts.method: The declared lists of workDeclarations laid out with the STATIC rule of 0x00D1E0F0 (booleans one bit, other members byte aligned, nesting and reserve entries at eight times their operand), arrays counted at count times the element width and nested lists offset by the start of their nesting member (both INFERRED).

workDeclarations.method: The declaration functions were executed on a minimal Lua 5.1 bytecode interpreter over the .le.lpb files of the installed client, decoded with tools/decode_lpb.py. Work members were replaced by recorders that capture each assignment to _save, _temp, _sync, _tag and _nesting. isMyPlayer, isPlayer and the _bindWork, _setTouchAttribute and nameplate natives were stubbed to record their arguments. No client code ran and no value comes from the executable.
workDeclarations.entryOrder: PlayerBaseClass._onInit calls ActorBaseClass.callSuperClassFunc('_onInit', true, true) first. CharaBaseClass._onInit therefore runs before any playerWork declaration, with its first flag true (declare the sync layouts) and its second flag true (declare the battle layouts).
workDeclarations.isMyPlayer: PlayerBaseClass.isMyPlayer returns whether worldMaster:_getMyPlayer() is self. CharaBaseClass.isPlayer returns nil and PlayerBaseClass.isPlayer returns true. CharaBaseClass._onInit sizes the nested members by isPlayer() and isMyPlayer(). When both hold, parameterSave, parameterTemp, battleSave and battleTemp get 512, 256, 512 and 128 bytes. Otherwise they get 64, 16, 64 and 16 bytes.
workDeclarations.memberEncoding: Each member is {name, type} with count for an array, bytes for a string, capacityBytes for a nesting entry, operand for a timer and reserveBytes for the _assignForChild reserve entry.

notMyPlayer.receiver: A PlayerBaseClass receiver for which isMyPlayer is false.
notMyPlayer.note: Such a receiver gets the chara declarations with the 64 and 16 byte nested members, one playerWork._sync member (_assignForChild), seven bind ids and no _setTouchAttribute call. The bind id 2002 binds battleSave.potencial and is made only on this path.

arguments.note: Attribute number. Only the low byte is kept and the scripts pass 1, 2 and 5. Bit a mod 32 of the byte is used when that count is below 8, otherwise no bit changes.
Selects which of two sets receives the attribute.

rows.behavior: Takes an attribute number and a bool and returns nothing. A PlayerBase receiver that is not a MyPlayer does nothing. The MyPlayer routine records the attribute in one of two ordered sets that hang off the object at MyPlayer +0x10C and, the first time an attribute is in neither set, sets bit (attribute mod 32) of the byte at +0x45C of the object at V +0x17838 when that count is below 8. It inserts the attribute into a set on every call. The flag never clears the bit. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x148]; jmp eax'. Slot 0x148 holds 0x00776340, which is 'ret 4', in the PlayerBase vftable (cell 0x00FD5F4C) and 0x006E6110 in the MyPlayer vftable (cell 0x00FD79A4).
The argument builder 0x0072BDC0 declares two entries. Entry 0 uses registry entry 0 (int) and entry 1 uses registry entry 2 (bool). The return list builder 0x0072B440 declares an empty list.

0x006E6110 reads cell 0 with the int reader 0x005819A0 and keeps the low byte, reads cell 1 with the bool reader 0x0071BA00 and selects the byte at 0x012D7C43 (the value 1 in the file) for true or the byte at 0x01355297 (uninitialized data) for false. The two bytes are the third argument of the call to 0x00895790.

When the dword at MyPlayer +0x10C is zero the routine allocates 0x18 bytes through 0x009D1B35, constructs them with 0x00895EF0 and stores the pointer there. The constructor builds two empty ordered sets of byte keys at object +0x00 and +0x0C through 0x0089AE80. The sets are ordered trees whose nodes hold a byte key at +0x0C and a nil flag at +0x0E.

0x00895790 finds the attribute in the set at +0x00 and in the set at +0x0C through 0x0089A1C0, an ordered set find. When both searches return the end node it calls 0x0075C950 with the attribute, which calls 0x00589720 on the object at V +0x17838 (0x004D72F0) with the flag 1. 0x00589720 computes 'mov dl,1; shl dl,cl' with cl the attribute byte (0x00589728) and ORs dl into the byte at +0x45C. An x86 shift masks its count to 5 bits, so the shifted byte is 0 when the attribute mod 32 is 8 or more and bit (attribute mod 32) otherwise: 0 to 7 set bits 0 to 7, 8 to 31 change nothing, 32 to 39 set bits 0 to 7 again, 40 to 63 change nothing, and so on up to the low byte 255. The clear branch (not dl, and) is reached only with a flag other than 1 and the only caller passes 1, so no path clears the bit. The routine then inserts the attribute through 0x0089A780 into the set at +0x00 when the flag byte equals the byte at 0x012D7C43 and into the set at +0x0C otherwise. The insert runs on every call (0x00895816..0x0089584F).

PlayerBaseClass._onInit calls the native six times, in this order and only when isMyPlayer is true: (1, true), (1, false), (2, true), (2, false), (5, true) and (5, false). The script has no other call, so the corpus passes the attribute numbers 1, 2 and 5 only.

The first sight of an attribute number raises its request bit in the byte at +0x45C. The object at V +0x17838 keeps three touch bytes cleared together by the reset at 0x0058BB87..0x0058BB93: +0x45C armed attributes, +0x45D attributes currently touched and +0x45E attributes whose touch start was reported. 0x005893F0 visits bits 0 to 5 only. For a bit armed in +0x45C it sets the +0x45E bit and calls virtual slot 0x54 (0x00574D50) of the object at this +0x80 when +0x45D has the bit and +0x45E does not, and clears the +0x45E bit and calls slot 0x58 (0x00574D60) when +0x45E has the bit and +0x45D does not. The roles come from this edge code and are INFERRED. The flag decides which set receives the attribute.

The readers of the two sets, the producer of the byte at +0x45D and the meaning of attribute numbers 1, 2 and 5. The byte +0x45D is stored by the async dispatcher 0x0058E0C0 for opcode 0x60 (0x0058E622, one byte from the payload pointer) and by the reset. The writers 0x00588200, 0x00588300 and 0x00588330 have no caller and no vftable reference. None of the 91 direct callers of the async enqueue 0x007CE7B0 pushes 0x60 as an immediate within ten instructions before the call.

corpusCallSites.sitesNote: Per-line sites are omitted for size. Rebuild them from the callsites list of this native in xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.

arguments.note: Attribute number. Only the low byte is kept.

returns.note: The bit of the attribute in the byte at +0x45D of the object at V +0x17838.

rows.behavior: Takes an attribute number and returns a bool. A PlayerBase receiver that is not a MyPlayer pushes nothing. The MyPlayer routine reports the bit of that attribute in the byte at +0x45D of the object at V +0x17838, except that attribute 1 answers false while the first node of a list on Y reports a nonzero byte. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk through slot 0x14C. The PlayerBase cell 0x00FD5F50 holds 0x00776340 ('ret 4') and the MyPlayer cell 0x00FD79A8 holds 0x00705320.

0x00705320 reads cell 0 with the int reader, keeps the low byte, calls 0x00894EE0 with the receiver identity and the address of the byte, and pushes the answer as a bool through 0x00748870 on the container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C. The routine does not read the sets at MyPlayer +0x10C.

0x00894EE0 resolves Y through 0x00CC7510. For the attribute 1 it calls 0x00763030 on Y and returns false when that answers true. Otherwise it calls 0x0075C970, which reaches 0x00589750 on the object at V +0x17838 and returns the bit of the attribute in the byte at +0x45D. 0x00763030 returns the byte at +0xBA of the object in the first node of the list at its receiver +0x1C, or 0 when the list at +0x20 is empty.

The bit test is 'mov edx,1; shl edx,cl; test byte [+0x45D],dl' (0x0058975B), so the count is masked to 5 bits and the tested mask is 0 when the attribute mod 32 is 8 or more. Attributes 0 to 7 test bits 0 to 7, 32 to 39 test bits 0 to 7 again, and every attribute whose remainder modulo 32 is 8 or more answers false.

The producer of the byte at +0x45D (the async dispatcher 0x0058E0C0 opcode 0x60 stores it and no direct pusher of 0x60 was found), the writers of the byte at +0xBA and the meaning of the list at +0x1C.

Member name in that work object.

rows.behavior: Takes a work name, a member name and an optional element range and returns nothing. It builds a request record from the names and the zero based range and hands it, with the receiver identity, to the object at Y +0xEC, which queues it or sends it through 0x00767C00. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument builder 0x0073CF80 declares four entries. Entries 0 and 1 use registry entry 3 (Utf8String). Entries 2 and 3 are built through 0x007271F0, which uses registry entry 0 (int). The return list builder 0x0072B440 declares an empty list.

The callback reads cells 0 and 1 with the string reader 0x0071CE70 and builds a request object through 0x0070AA10, which copies the first string to object +0x00 and the second to +0x54 and zeroes the words at +0xA8 and +0xAA. When the tag byte at cell 2 (+0x2C) is not 6 it reads cells 2 and 3 with the int reader, subtracts 1 from each, keeps 16 bits of each and rebuilds the request through 0x0070AAA0 and 0x006CE1C0.

0x006E7819 resolves Y through 0x00CC7510, loads the object at Y +0xEC and calls 0x00767FC0 with ExecuteParameters +0x04, the receiver identity at ExecuteParameters +0x0C and the request. 0x00767FC0 resolves a record through 0x0071D420. When the byte at record +0x29 is zero it calls 0x00767C00 directly. Otherwise it appends the request to a deque at this +0x24 through 0x007838C0 when the deque is empty, and then calls 0x00767C00, or takes the path at 0x00768024 when the deque holds entries.

The CharaBase script calls the native with ('charaWork', member) and with ('charaWork', 'commandAcquired', first - 26000, last - 26000). Each call sits behind a canRequestInformation() guard on the local player and is followed by recordRequestInformation(). The Player script calls it with ('work', a, b, c) and the PlayerBase script with ('playerWork', a, b, c) in the same guard. The corpus has 7 call sites in 6 scripts for all four registrations.

The request asks the client service at Y +0xEC to refresh one work member. The ranges are zero based on the native side because both cells have 1 subtracted. The role comes from the guard calls, the names and the shared request record. The packet that 0x00767C00 sends, if any, was not traced.
Whether 0x00767C00 emits a client packet, which one, and what happens to a request that is queued behind another.

rows.behavior: Takes three floats. It builds the world position record of the receiver, takes atan2 with the x difference as the numerator and the z difference as the denominator, subtracts the receiver heading and folds the result into the range around zero. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument builder 0x0073CE40 declares three float entries and the return builder 0x0072B390 declares one float entry. The callback reads cell 0 and cell 2 with the float reader 0x0071BAC0. It never reads cell 1.

0x006F9B9F resolves the identity at ExecuteParameters +0x0C and calls 0x0075C230 with a 0x10 byte record, the same position record as _getPosition and _getDirection. The code subtracts record +0x00 from x and record +0x08 from z, calls 0x009DAEBA with the two differences and subtracts the record float at +0x0C from the result.

The fold adds the double pi at 0x00F62F48 when the angle is at or above zero and subtracts it below zero, divides by 2 pi at 0x00F62FE0, truncates the quotient and subtracts the truncated multiple of 2 pi. The float is pushed through 0x007489D0.

0x009DAEBA loads the descriptor 0x012EBB80, whose name field is 'atan2', and jumps to the two operand CRT dispatcher 0x009ECA10. The routine that does the work (0x009EC97C) takes the absolute values of both operands, runs fpatan and corrects the quadrant from the signs. fpatan computes atan(ST1 / ST0). The callback loads the x difference first and the z difference second, so the result is atan2(dx, dz). The entry order of the dispatcher is the MSVC _CIatan2 convention (ST1 first operand) and is INFERRED. The result is the bearing from the receiver to the point, 0 along +z and growing toward +x, relative to the record heading.

The heading fold computes in doubles a + pi for a at or above 0 and a - pi below 0 (0x00F62F48 holds 3.1415927410125732), divides by 0x00F62FE0 (6.2831854820251465), truncates the quotient toward zero to an int n with cvttsd2si, converts n to a float and back and returns a - n * 2pi rounded to a float. An angle strictly between -pi and pi is unchanged. The endpoints swap: pi returns -pi and -pi returns pi. A nonnegative angle lands in [-pi, pi), a negative one in (-pi, pi], and an unordered compare takes the below zero branch.

Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time.

The Lua bytecode facts come from the installed client scripts. Their sources are not redistributed, and the tracked script metadata holds names and line numbers only. The declared member names, types and counts are recorded here as metadata of those scripts.

The declaration lists come from a stub interpreter over the bytecode. The interpreter implements the instructions that the declaration functions use and replaces the native work members, so it checks the lists the scripts build and not the client behavior around them.

The work binder facts describe the Lua layer, the layout rule and the bind records. The pool objects behind the read and write accessors, the initial member values, the array count rule, the origin of nested lists, the array index base of the readers and the callers of the by-id accessors were not traced.
The callbacks that dereference a resolved identity or a lookup result without a test were not run with an absent identity, so their run-time effect is unknown.
The invalid-parameter route ends in a process terminate on the evidence of the target cursor contract. The calls that reach it with an out-of-range member position or a missing cell were not run.
These are client marshalling and state contracts. They do not establish work member values, group membership, touch states, region ids or server behavior.
